bull.b: Broad-based growth across oncology, rare sleep and established brands supports a durable expansion trend. The raised full-year outlook indicates management sees commercial momentum continuing beyond a single quarter.

Strong operating cash flow and substantial liquidity improve Jazz’s ability to fund clinical development, acquisitions and debt obligations. Reduced leverage also increases financial flexibility if operating conditions become less favorable.

The first-line approval expands Ziihera’s addressable patient population and strengthens Jazz’s oncology presence. Its survival data and multiple approved regimens provide a foundation for broader commercial adoption and future indication expansion.

bear.b: The recent profitability recovery is encouraging, but repeated loss years show that earnings remain sensitive to product mix, impairments and development spending. This history reduces confidence that current margins will persist through the cycle.

Higher royalties on oncology products and increased commercial and clinical investment can limit operating leverage. Sustained spending may be strategically necessary, but it creates a continuing risk that revenue growth will not translate proportionally into profit.

Potential generic and novel-mechanism competition could pressure the established oxybate franchise, while the Zepzelca label change may accelerate erosion in its second-line business. These risks could weaken the durability of key revenue streams.
